done.why: I reached the troll unarmed after a short run through rooms I already knew. The prose was terse, so I stopped.

about: A text adventure that looks like the classic Zork. You start outside a white house, get in through the kitchen window, take the lamp, move the rug, go down the trap door and meet a troll in the cellars.

moments.note: 'With great effort, you open the window far enough to allow entry.' A nice small bit of effort in the wording.
The trap door crashes shut and you hear someone barring it. It is a good ominous beat.
'examine walls' got 'You can't see any such thing', even though the room text describes the walls.
Examining the troll only repeated the room description.

wished: To examine the scenery that the room descriptions mention, such as the walls.
To get more detail from 'examine' than the room text already gave.

lines.line: The trap door crashes shut, and you hear someone barring it.
lines.why: It is the best moment of atmosphere, and it gives a sudden sense of being trapped.

lines.line: A nasty-looking troll, brandishing a bloody axe, blocks all passages out of the room.
lines.why: It is a strong, compact threat.

fun.why: It is a smooth, responsive run, but familiar.

engagement.why: It moved quickly, but I stopped once I was blocked by the troll.

difficulty.why: The early steps were straightforward and the parser accepted most of what I typed.

interestingness.why: The setting is well known, and I saw little that was new.

prose.why: The prose is crisp and economical, with good small touches, but examining things gave little extra.
